# Phase 0 — building the knowledge base

Before finding a single creator, the engine needed to know what "good" looks like in French reselling. The first attempt was not good enough, and I said so.

---

## Choosing the research substrate before writing the agent

`2026-07-09T12:58:11.019Z` · session `89990030` · branch `main`

**The engine put a decision to Doug, and he answered:**

> **Q.** What should the research skill actually search with, to start? (Biggest build decision — it's *why* Reddit/forums came back thin on the Fleek run: plain WebFetch gets blocked by Reddit.)
>
> **A.** Perplexity from the start
>
> **Q.** How much do we build in this first pass?
>
> **A.** build the skill - to research skill that is going to extrapolate and enrich a wiki base regardless of its category and project. And yeah, so what that means is, you know, when the skill has been activated, you know, we need to have a procedure and, you know, what we're looking for and why. The purpose, yeah, so let's build the research skill out, which we can then activate when we're trying to enrich a wiki base, esp…
>

**What changed because of it:** Plain WebFetch was being blocked by Reddit, so the wiki was coming back thin. Committing to Perplexity as the search substrate up front — rather than discovering the block later — is why the wiki has cited sources instead of hallucinated ones.

## Killing two agents in favour of one reusable skill

`2026-07-09T13:22:29.244Z` · session `89990030` · branch `main`

**What Doug typed, verbatim:**

> delete scout and brain research agent. 
>
> rename skill to wiki knowledge base builder

**What changed because of it:** I had asked for a research agent; the model built two, each welded to Fleek. I deleted both. What replaced them — the `wiki-knowledge-base-builder` skill — is project-agnostic and has since been pointed at other domains. The brief asks for something that "would still work if France was 500 creators instead of 10." This is that, one level up: it works if the project isn't Fleek.

## Injecting the word the model didn't know it needed

`2026-07-09T14:04:12.536Z` · session `7dc7ed35` · branch `wiki-knowledge-base-research-aa1c1d`

**What Doug typed, verbatim:**

> go -  dont forget "friperie" french localised term for vintage / thrift

**What changed because of it:** "Friperie" is what French resellers actually call thrift. No amount of English-language reasoning surfaces it. It became a core search keyword, a scoring signal, and the tonal anchor for the French outreach drafts. Domain knowledge the human supplies is still the scarce input.

## Rejecting the research agent's entire first output

`2026-07-09T16:03:03.474Z` · session `7dc7ed35` · branch `wiki-knowledge-base-research-aa1c1d`

**What Doug typed, verbatim:**

> We're going to the Obsidian Vault, where we have a wiki-based building. And quite frankly, I don't think it's rich enough. The research task doesn't seem to have populated the wiki base with enough material, and I don't really know why. But yeah, I would like to enrich further, please.
>
> https://styleparis.substack.com/p/the-only-paris-second-hand-shopping

**What came back:**

> Two things here — a source to mine, and a fair question about *why* the vault feels thin. Let me address the "why" honestly first, then fetch your Substack. **Why it feels thin:** the sweep used Perplexity `sonar`, which is a *summariser*, not a deep extractor. It returns 1–3k-char syntheses and, for niche FR queries, often came back with "no data found" (the lanes I flagged). It never deep-reads an individual page. The richest FR material — named shops, neighbourhoods, insider detail — lives in…

**What changed because of it:** The agent reported success. The vault was thin. I rejected the whole run rather than build on it, and supplied a primary source to work from instead. That triggered the deep-read enrichment method — reading sources directly rather than synthesising summaries of them — which is where the vault's best pages came from.
